title: Answers reorder media sections and omit unsupported tracks
test: tests/whip.test.js: 'WHIP answer for an audio-first offer lists the sections in offer order', 'WHIP answer rejects an audio section with no supported codec with port 0 in place', 'WHIP answer rejects an application section with port 0 and keeps the other mids', 'WHIP accepts only the first supported section of each kind and rejects the others' (plus 'WHIP answer for a video-first OBS offer keeps both accepted sections and their attributes', a regression guard that passed before the fix)
proof: Before the fix, node --test tests/whip.test.js failed 4 of 10. Audio-first offer (audio mid 0, video mid 1): answer listed m=video then m=audio with a=group:BUNDLE 1 0. Offer of H.264 video and PCMU/PCMA audio: answer had 1 m-line for 2 offered (expected 2, actual 1); the audio section was dropped instead of rejected. Offer of video, m=application, audio: parsed.video.mid was '1', because the parser did not recognise m=application and applied that section's a=mid to the video section before it; the answer then had 2 m-lines for 3, with BUNDLE 1 2. Two H.264 video sections: the later one replaced the earlier, so parsed.video.mid was '1' and the answer had 2 m-lines for 3. After the fix, parseOffer records every m-section in offer order (index, kind, port, proto, formats, mid), keeps parsedOffer.video and .audio as the first section of each kind with a supported codec, and createAnswer emits one section per offered section in offer order: the accepted ones as before, every other one as m=<kind> 0 <offered proto> <first offered format> with c=, the offered a=mid and a=inactive, no ICE, DTLS or candidate lines, and left out of a=group:BUNDLE. All 10 tests pass, and the full suite passes 505 of 505. Compared against the unchanged lib/whip.js on a video-first offer, a video-only offer and an audio-first offer in OBS style (session-level ICE and DTLS, ssrc, msid, rtcp-fb, stereo Opus, in H.264 and AV1 rooms): producer rtpParameters, parseDtlsParameters and validateCodecs are identical; each accepted section's lines are identical; video-first and video-only answers are byte-identical apart from the o= timestamp; the audio-first answer differs only in section and BUNDLE order.
